article.title: Hit the books
article.description: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).
article.content: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).

generated.caption:
Got a big exam coming up? 📚 When you need to study hard, especially before a test, you "hit the books"! This informal idiom is very common among students.

For example: "I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test."

generated.script:
Aapko bhi lagta hai 'hit the books' matlab kitabon ko marna? Toh ye reel aapke liye hai!

Toh, 'hit the books' ka matlab hai to study hard, usually before an exam. Matlab, bohot zyada padhai karna, khaaskar exam se pehle. Ye students mein bohot common hai. For example, 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Yaani, 'Main aaj bahar nahi ja sakta, mujhe kal ke test ke liye bohot padhna hai.'

Toh jab next time koi bole 'hit the books', toh samajh jaana ki wo exam ke liye bohot mehnat se padhne jaa raha hai. Ab confusion clear ho gayi na?

slides.headlineRest: — What It Means to Study Hard
slides.body: To 'hit the books' is an informal idiom that means to study hard, usually in preparation for an exam. This phrase is very common among students when they need to dedicate serious time to their studies. For example, you might hear someone say, 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' It's somewhat similar to 'cram for an exam,' which implies studying very intensively, often at the last minute.
